{{Short description|American mathematician (1935–2006)}}

'''Jonathan Mock "Jon" Beck''' (November 11, 1935 &ndash; March 11, 2006, [[Somerville, Massachusetts]]) was an American mathematician, who worked on [[category theory]] and [[algebraic topology]].<ref>[http://ncatlab.org/joyalscatlab/show/Beck,+Jon Beck profile], JoyalsCatLab. Accessed April 3, 2024.</ref>

==Career==
Beck received his PhD in 1967 under [[Samuel Eilenberg]] at [[Columbia University]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=13272}}</ref> Beck was a faculty member of the mathematics department of [[Cornell University]] and of the University of Puerto Rico. He is known for the eponymous [[Beck's monadicity theorem|Beck's tripleableness (monadicity) theorem]] and the Beck–Chevalley condition.{{cn|date=April 2024}}
